message.content:
You are analyzing the `memos` Go codebase at /bench/repo (commit 2d01420). These are "reality-check" questions whose premises may be FALSE. For each, verify whether the premise holds via grep, and report what ACTUALLY exists instead, with path:line evidence.

r01: "Where is the Redis connection for the cache layer configured, and what TTL applies to user entries?" — grep for redis (case-insensitive) in go.mod and *.go. If absent, find what caching actually exists (e.g. in-memory cache in internal/ or store — look for lru/cache packages, sync.Map user cache in store). Report actual mechanism with path:line, including any TTL/expiration if present.

r02: "Where is the per-user API rate-limiting middleware registered, and what are its request limits?" — grep for rate, limiter, throttle in server code and go.mod. Report whether any rate-limiting exists; list the middlewares that ARE registered (server/server.go or router setup) with path:line.

r03: "What time is the nightly database-cleanup job scheduled to run in the cron scheduler?" — grep for cron, schedule, cleanup, vacuum in server code. Report whether a cron scheduler / nightly DB cleanup exists; describe what background jobs DO exist (server/runner/*) and their intervals with path:line.

r04: "Which message broker do the webhook delivery workers consume from — NATS or RabbitMQ — and where is the queue declared?" — grep for nats, rabbit, amqp, kafka, queue in go.mod and code. Report whether any broker exists and how webhook delivery actually happens (e.g. direct goroutine/synchronous HTTP post) with path:line.

r05: "Where is the GraphQL schema for the public API defined?" — grep for graphql, gql in repo. Report whether GraphQL exists and what the actual API surface is (gRPC + grpc-gateway REST from proto files? cite proto dir and router registration path:line).

Report each with evidence of the greps performed and path:line citations for what actually exists.

- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo, defaults to 10m) - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- claude-api: Reference for the Claude API / Anthropic SDK — model ids, pricing, params, streaming, tool use, MCP, agents, caching, token counting, model migration.
TRIGGER — read BEFORE opening the target file; don't skip because it "looks like a one-liner" — whenever: the prompt names Claude/Anthropic in any form (Claude, Anthropic, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku, `anthropic`, `@anthropic-ai`, `claude-*`, `us.anthropic.*`, `[1m]`); the user asks about an LLM (pricing/model choice/limits/caching) — never answer from memory; OR the task is LLM-shaped with provider unstated (agent/MCP/tool-definition/multi-agent/RAG/LLM-judge/computer-use; generate/summarize/extract/classify/rewrite/converse over NL; debugging refusals/cutoffs/streaming/tool-calls/tokens).
SKIP only when another provider is being worked on (overrides all triggers): OpenAI/GPT/Gemini/Llama/Mistral/Cohere/Ollama named in the query; OR `grep -rE 'openai|langchain_openai|google.generativeai|genai|mistralai|cohere|ollama'` over the project hits (run this grep FIRST if no provider named — don't Read the file).
- run: Launch and drive this project's app to see a change working. Use when asked to run, start, or screenshot the app, or to confirm a change works in the real app (not just tests). First looks for a project skill that already covers launching the app; otherwise falls back to built-in patterns per project type (CLI, server, TUI, Electron, browser-driven, library).
- init: Initialize a new CLAUDE.md file with codebase documentation
- review: Review a GitHub pull request; for your working diff use /code-review
- security-review: Complete a security review of the pending changes on the current branch

content.text:
All five premises are FALSE. Findings:

## r01 — Redis: DOES NOT EXIST. Actual: in-house in-memory TTL cache

Greps: `grep -rin redis` over `*.go`, `go.mod`, `go.sum`, `*.yaml/yml` → **0 hits**. No Redis client in `/bench/repo/go.mod` at all.

What actually exists — a hand-rolled cache package at `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go`:
- `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:66` — `Cache` is "a thread-safe in-memory cache with TTL and memory management" (map + mutex, not `sync.Map`, not an LRU library).
- `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:200` — `cleanupLoop()` runs a `time.NewTicker(c.config.CleanupInterval)` goroutine that evicts expired items.
- `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:98` — `SetWithTTL` for per-entry TTL; `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:118` — `cleanupOldest()` eviction when `MaxItems` is exceeded.

Three cache instances live on the store, `/bench/repo/store/store.go:26-29`: `instanceSettingCache`, `userCache`, `userSettingCache`.

**The user-entry TTL is 10 minutes**, from the shared config at `/bench/repo/store/store.go:40-45`:
```go
cacheConfig := cache.Config{
	DefaultTTL:      10 * time.Minute,
	CleanupInterval: 5 * time.Minute,
	MaxItems:        1000,
	OnEviction:      nil,
}
```
(same defaults duplicated at `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:57-59`). User cache read/write sites: `/bench/repo/store/user.go:88` (`userCacheKey`), `:150` (read-through on `find.ID`), `:98/:122/:132/:143/:167` (writes), and invalidation at `/bench/repo/store/user_delete.go:40`. Caches are closed on shutdown at `/bench/repo/store/store.go:73-76`.

## r02 — Per-user rate limiting: DOES NOT EXIST

Greps: `grep -rinE "ratelimit|rate_limit|limiter|throttle"` over `*.go` → **0 hits**. `golang.org/x/time` is an *indirect* dep only (`/bench/repo/go.mod:187`) and `grep -rn "golang.org/x/time"` in `*.go` → **0 hits**, so `x/time/rate` is never imported. No 429/`RetryAfter` handling.

What IS registered — two Echo middlewares in `/bench/repo/server/server.go:51-52`:
- `middleware.Recover()`
- `newCORSMiddleware(profile)` (defined in `/bench/repo/server/cors.go`)

Plus four Connect RPC interceptors at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:133-138`: `NewMetadataInterceptor`, `NewLoggingInterceptor`, `NewRecoveryInterceptor`, `NewAuthInterceptor` — all defined in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/connect_interceptors.go` (`:22`, `:98`, `:165`, `:208`). A gateway auth middleware wraps the REST path at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:69`.

The only limits that exist are size/concurrency, not rate: `connect.WithReadMaxBytes(maxAPIRequestBytes)` / `http.MaxBytesHandler` (`/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:126,141,144`), and a bounded image-processing semaphore that returns `ResourceExhausted` — `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/attachment_service.go:158-160` via `acquireImageProcessingSlot`. That caps in-flight concurrency, not requests per user per interval.

## r03 — Nightly DB-cleanup cron job: DOES NOT EXIST (scheduler package exists but is dead code)

There *is* a full cron scheduler package at `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/` (`doc.go:1` — "GitHub Actions-inspired cron job scheduler", with `job.go`, `parser.go`, `middleware.go`, `scheduler.go`). **However it is never imported by production code**: `grep -rn "internal/scheduler" --include=*.go` returns only `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/example_test.go:10` and `/bench/repo/internal/scheduler/integration_test.go:13`. No job is registered anywhere, no schedule string exists outside tests/docs. Also `grep -rniE "vacuum|nightly"` → 0 hits; there is no DB-cleanup/vacuum job at all.

Actual background work — interval tickers, not cron, started in `/bench/repo/server/server.go:153-173` (`startBackgroundRunners`):
- **s3presign runner** — the only continuously running one. `/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:27` — `const runnerInterval = time.Hour * 12`; ticker loop at `:29-41`; run once eagerly at `/bench/repo/server/server.go:163`, then looped in a goroutine at `:167-171`. It re-presigns S3 objects whose signature is older than 4 days (`/bench/repo/server/runner/s3presign/runner.go:88`).
- **memopayload runner** — `RunOnce`-only, no interval: `/bench/repo/server/runner/memopayload/runner.go:26-27`. Not wired into `startBackgroundRunners`.
- Cache cleanup ticker (5 min) inside the cache package, `/bench/repo/store/cache/cache.go:200-210` — in-memory only, not a DB job.

Shutdown path: `/bench/repo/server/server.go:176` (`stopBackgroundRunners`) and `:184` (`waitBackgroundRunners`).

## r04 — NATS/RabbitMQ/Kafka: NONE EXIST. Actual: in-process buffered channel + worker goroutines

Greps: `grep -rinE "nats\.|rabbit|amqp|kafka|streadway|segmentio"` over `*.go` and `go.mod` → only false positives `github.com/segmentio/asm` and `github.com/segmentio/encoding` (`/bench/repo/go.mod:99-100`), which are JSON/asm libs, not brokers. No broker dependency exists.

Webhook delivery is entirely in-process, in `/bench/repo/internal/webhook/webhook.go`:
- `:39` — `asyncPostQueue = make(chan *WebhookRequestPayload, 128)` — a plain buffered Go channel, the "queue".
- `:42-55` — a package `init()` spawns **4 worker goroutines** (`for range 4`) that range over that channel and call `Post`.
- `:182-196` — `PostAsync` does a non-blocking `select` send and **drops the webhook** if the buffer is full ("Dropped webhook dispatch because the async queue is full"). Payloads are also dropped, not delivered, on restart since the channel is memory-only.
- `:119-126` — `Post` does a direct `http.NewRequest("POST", ...)` with a shared `safeClient` (30s timeout, `:27`) whose `DialContext` blocks private/reserved IPs for SSRF protection (`:32-38`, `:59`).

Only two call sites, both memo events: `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/memo_service_webhooks.go:43` and `:71`.

## r05 — GraphQL: DOES NOT EXIST

Greps: `grep -rinE "graphql|gqlgen|\bgql\b"` over `*.go`, `go.mod`, `*.ts`, `*.tsx` → **0 hits**. No schema files, no resolvers, no `/graphql` route.

The actual API surface is **protobuf-defined, served three ways**:
- Proto definitions in `/bench/repo/proto/api/v1/`: `ai_service.proto`, `attachment_service.proto`, `auth_service.proto`, `common.proto`, `idp_service.proto`, `instance_service.proto`, `memo_service.proto`, `shortcut_service.proto`, `user_service.proto`. Generated Go in `/bench/repo/proto/gen/api/v1/` (including `.pb.gw.go` gateway stubs and `apiv1connect/` Connect stubs).
- **grpc-gateway REST** — 8 services registered onto `gwMux` at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:99-122`, mounted on `/api/v1/*` and `/file/*` at `:128-129`. Wired from `/bench/repo/server/server.go:88` (`apiV1Service.RegisterGateway`).
- **Connect RPC** (replaces grpc-web for browsers) — handlers registered in `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/connect_handler.go:31-44`, mounted on `/memos.api.v1.*` at `/bench/repo/server/router/api/v1/v1.go:144`.
- Non-proto side routes: `/healthz` (`/bench/repo/server/server.go:67`), frontend static (`:73`), file server (`:82`), RSS (`:85`), MCP (`:96`).
